title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Lena Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the standard process and operational guardrails for: onboarding models into the Applied ML Eval Harness, constructing and validating prompt sets and benchmarks, selecting quantization profiles, and performing regression triage. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML specialists, and SREs who own runtime regressions and quality monitoring.

Scope
- Eval harness onboarding (integration tests, CI, and Canary evaluation)
- Prompt sets and benchmark lifecycle (creation, review, and maintenance)
- Quality guardrails (metrics, thresholds, and automated alerts)
- Quantization profiles (selection, validation, and rollback)
- Regression triage playbook (prioritization, mitigation, and RCA)

Terminology
- Eval harness: the CI + periodic evaluation system that runs prompt-set-driven tests against candidate and production models.
- Prompt set: curated examples used to measure model quality for a specific vertical or feature.
- Regression: any statistically significant degradation in a tracked metric (accuracy, factuality, latency, hallucinations).
- Quantization profile: configuration that specifies bit-width, per-channel vs per-tensor, and supported kernels.

Owner and SLAs
- Primary owner: Applied ML (applied-ml-and-evals)
- Secondary owner: Eng-SRE (for infra and reliability)
- Onboarding SLA: 10 business days from defect-free artifact upload to first CI pass (experimental models may take longer)
- Regression response SLA: 48h initial analysis, 7-day mitigation or rollback plan

1) Eval Harness Onboarding Checklist
Follow this checklist when bringing a new model into the eval harness. Each step is required unless explicitly waived by the applied-ml lead.

1. Prepare artifacts
   - Model artifact (container image or HF tarball) with semantic versioning (semver-like tag).
   - Model card: includes architecture, training data summary, license, privacy notes, and intended use cases.
   - Inference config JSON: tokenizer, max_sequence_length, batching hints, KV cache support, supported quantization profiles.

2. Local validation (pre-CI)
   - Run eval-harness local runner: `tools/eval_harness/run_local.sh --model <model_uri> --prompt-set smoke`
   - Confirm deterministic outputs for the smoke prompt set (same seed, same version).

3. CI integration
   - Submit PR to `eval-harness/configs` with model entry and inference config.
   - Ensure CI job `eval-harness/on-commit` passes all smoke checks.

4. Canary evaluation
   - Schedule a canary run against the full prompt sets for the target workload.
   - Canary window: 24h for high-priority workloads, 72h for lower priority.

5. Sign-off
   - Applied ML approver and an SRE reviewer must sign the canary results page.

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks: Creation & Review
Design prompts to represent real product usage and common edge cases. Each prompt set must have metadata.

Required metadata fields for each prompt set (CSV/JSON):
- id (short string)
- owner_team
- intent (short description)
- dataset_size (examples count)
- difficulty_profile (easy|medium|hard)
- creation_date
- upstream_data_source (if any)

Prompt set lifecycle
- Draft -> Internal Review -> Approved -> Archived
- Reviewers: Product PM, Applied ML engineer, Data privacy reviewer (if dataset includes customer data)

Benchmark scoring guidelines
- Use task-specific metrics where possible (ROUGE/BLEU for summarization, F1/EM for extraction, accuracy for classification, MRR for retrieval-augmented ranking).
- Also track: hallucination rate, toxic-content flag rate, and latency P50/P95/P99.

Example benchmark table (canonical SLOs):
| metric               | target SLO        | alert threshold |
|----------------------|-------------------:|----------------:|
| task_accuracy        | 90%               | drop > 3pp      |
| hallucination_rate   | < 2%              | > 5%            |
| latency_p95          | < 200 ms (small)  | > 300 ms        |
| latency_p95 (large)  | < 500 ms          | > 750 ms        |
| inference_cost_per_1k_tokens | <= $0.80   | increase > 20%  |

3) Model Onboarding Procedure (step-by-step)
A reproducible, auditable process reduces risk. Follow these steps: 

1. Pre-onboarding review
   - Confirm license and training data constraints.
   - Confirm any export control or privacy restrictions.

2. Artifact upload and scanning
   - Upload to artifact registry: `artifacts.redwood.internal/models/<team>/<model>:<tag>`
   - Automated security scanner runs (SBOM, suspicious packages).

3. CI & Eval config PR
   - Add entry to `eval-harness/configs/models.json` and `prompt-sets/` references.

4. Canary + Shadow testing
   - Run in shadow mode against production traffic for 24-72 hours. Shadow logs collected to `s3://redwood-eval-shadow/<model>/<date>/`

5. Approval gates
   - Signed checklist: privacy, security, applied-ml quality, SRE stability.

4) Quality Guardrails and Automated Alerts
Set conservative guardrails to detect silent regressions early. Key signals: metric deltas, distribution shift, latency, and cost anomalies.

Automated alerting configuration (examples):
- Alert: `eval_accuracy_drop`
  - Trigger: rolling 3-day drop in task_accuracy > 2 percentage points AND p-value < 0.05
  - Notify: applied-ml-oncall, model-owner, eng-sre
- Alert: `latency_sla_breach`
  - Trigger: p95 latency > SLO for 30m window
  - Notify: eng-sre, infra oncall

Suggested thresholds (tune per workload):
- accuracy: alert on >2pp drop, pager on >5pp drop
- hallucination_rate: alert on >2x baseline, pager on >5x baseline
- latency p95: alert on 20% increase, pager on 50% increase

5) Quantization Profiles: selection and validation
Quantization reduces cost but can introduce quality regressions. Documented profiles must include validation steps.

Profile naming convention: `<precision>-<granularity>-<kernel-compat>` e.g., `int8-per-channel-fused-kernel-v1`

Profile metadata (required):
- name
- bit_width
- per_channel (true/false)
- supported_kernels (comma-separated list)
- expected_memory_savings (estimated percent)
- recommended_workloads (chat|completion|embedding)

Quantization validation checklist:
1. Baseline evaluation: run full prompt-set benchmarks on FP16/FP32 baseline.
2. Quantized run: run identical benchmarks with quantized profile.
3. Delta analysis: compute metric deltas (accuracy, hallucination, factuality).
4. A/B evaluation in canary: 24-72h with traffic split (5-20%).
5. Rollout policy: gradually increase traffic to target with automated rollback on regressions.

Rollback criteria (example):
- any task_accuracy drop > 3pp OR hallucination_rate > 3x baseline -> immediate rollback
- cost savings < 10% after rollout window -> consider disabling profile

6) Regression Triage Playbook
When an alert fires, follow this procedure to rapidly assess impact and remediate.

Initial triage (0-48h):
1. Acknowledge and assemble incident lead (applied-ml oncall) and model owner.
2. Collect artifacts: failing prompt examples, baseline outputs, canary runs, recent deploys, infra metrics (GPU memory, kernel errors).
3. Run targeted local reproducer: `tools/eval_harness/reproduce --model <model> --prompt-id <id> --seed <seed>`
4. Classify the regression: data drift, model change, quantization effect, infra degradation, or prompt parsing error.
5. If classification == infra degradation -> engage eng-sre and consider traffic migration.

Mitigation (24-72h):
- If model change: roll back to previous tag and reopen PR for investigation.
- If quantization: disable quantized profile and revert to baseline.
- If data drift: throttle model and trigger dataset refresh / retrain pipeline.

Root Cause Analysis (post-mitigation, 3-14 days):
- Produce RCA doc with timeline, reproducer, fix, and preventive actions.
- Owners: applied-ml produces fix; eng-sre verifies infra fixes.

Postmortem template (required fields)
- summary
- impact and customer-facing effects
- timeline of events
- root cause(s) and contributing factors
- corrective actions (short and long term)
- metrics and dashboards changed
- verification plan and closure criteria

7) Automation and CI hooks
Recommended CI jobs and frequency:
- `eval-harness/on-commit` (smoke): run on every model PR (fast tests)
- `eval-harness/full-bench` (nightly): run full prompt sets nightly for active models
- `eval-harness/regression-detect` (daily): compute change point detection and generate alerts

Useful commands and snippets
- Run a single prompt locally:
  tools/eval_harness/run_single.sh --model artifacts.redwood.internal/models/nlp/gpt-like:1.3.0 --prompt-id prompt_1234

- Compare baseline vs candidate outputs (example JSON diff tool):
  python tools/eval_harness/compare_outputs.py --baseline outputs/baseline.json --candidate outputs/candidate.json --metrics accuracy,bleu,hallucination

Appendix: Example evaluation config (YAML)
model: artifacts.redwood.internal/models/nlp/gpt-like:1.3.0
prompt_sets:
  - id: customer-support-quality
    weight: 1.0
quantization_profile: int8-per-channel-fused-kernel-v1
metrics:
  - name: task_accuracy
  - name: hallucination_rate
  - name: latency_p95
schedule:
  nightly: true
  canary_window_hours: 24
